name: RBI Grade B
fullName: Reserve Bank of India – Officers in Grade 'B' (DR) General: Phase I
eligibility: Graduate with ≥60% (55% for SC/ST/PwBD) or post-graduate with ≥55% (pass for SC/ST/PwBD); 21–30 years (relaxations apply); limited number of attempts for the General stream

notification.summary: The 2026 cycle (≈60 posts: ≈40 General, ≈10 DEPR, ≈10 DSIM as reported) is in its final stage: Phase I for the General stream was held on 13 Jun 2026 and Phase II on 25 Jul 2026; the Phase II result/interview shortlist was reported in Aug 2026 and the final result was awaited in late Sep 2026. The next notification is expected around Apr–May 2027. Dates are from education portals; the RBI site could not be opened from the research environment.

pattern.notes: Sectional timing (approx.): GA 25 min, Reasoning 45 min, English 25 min, Quant 25 min. Sectional and aggregate cut-offs apply; Phase I is qualifying only. Phase II has three papers (Economic & Social Issues, English writing, Finance & Management) followed by an interview (Phase II + interview decide the merit).

trendAnalysis.summary: Phase I is moderate overall; reasoning (puzzles of 5–6 sets: square/circular tables, box, floor, year/age-based) is the most time-consuming and was rated moderate-to-difficult in 2026. GA carries 80 marks and is dominated by 6–8 months of current affairs on banking, RBI policy, economy, government schemes, international reports and appointments; static questions are few. Quant is DI-heavy (missing-data tables, caselets) and in 2026 swapped quadratic equations for simplification/approximation. English (RC, cloze, error spotting, fillers, para-jumbles) was easier than 2025. Overall good attempts were reported around 100–115 with cut-offs near 100 ± 5.

pyqBlueprint.method: Compiled from memory-based analyses of RBI Grade B (General) Phase I 2024 (Sept 2024) and 2025 (18 Oct 2025) published by coaching sites (Bankersadda, PracticeMock, C4S Courses, Mahendras), cross-checked against the official Phase I pattern (GA 80, Reasoning 60, English 30, Quant 30). GA archetypes are framed around recurring themes (RBI Act provisions, regulatory circulars, payment systems, schemes, reports) rather than specific current-affairs items. Patterns are paraphrased; no real question is reproduced.

archetypes.pattern: RC set (450–600 words) on monetary policy, banking or the economy: central idea / author's main concern; distractors are partial or overstated claims
RC fact-check: 'Which of the following is true / NOT true according to the passage' — one option distorts a qualifier (some→most, may→will) or reverses cause and effect
RC inference with statements I, II, III and combination options (Only I / Only I and III …); the trap statement overstates what the passage says
RC vocabulary-in-context: synonym or antonym of a word used in the passage, with distractors that are dictionary meanings not fitting the context
Passage cloze with numbered blanks; five same-part-of-speech options where distractors are look-alike or collocation-breaking words
Sentence split into parts (A)–(D) plus 'No error' (E); errors in subject–verb agreement, prepositions, pronouns, tense, comparatives, or inversion after negative adverbs
Choose the grammatically correct (or incorrect) sentence among five similar sentences on one theme
Double filler: two blanks in one sentence, five word-pairs where one word of each wrong pair fits but the other does not
Single filler: one blank, five words close in meaning; only one matches the tone/collocation of the sentence
Para jumble of five or six sentences on one theme; choose the correct order (options are sequences); connectors like 'however', 'as a result' and pronouns fix the order
Para jumble asking which sentence comes FIRST / THIRD / LAST after rearrangement (options are sentence letters)
Standalone synonym/antonym of a moderately advanced word; distractors include words of the opposite sense
Meaning of an idiom/phrasal verb used in a sentence; distractors are literal readings
Table DI (5 rows × 2–3 columns): percentage increase/decrease of one entity between two years, or one entity as a percentage of another
Table DI on banking/corporate data (deposits, advances, revenue, expenditure %): derived ratios such as credit–deposit ratio, profit, or projected values after percentage growth
Caselet DI: a paragraph giving a total and splits in ratios/percentages; questions combine two splits or ask what changes after a transfer
Pie-chart DI (shares in % or degrees of a total): find values, differences and ratios across sectors
Bar/line-graph DI (values given for 5–6 categories or months): averages, ratios and percentage differences
Two quadratic equations in x and y with integer/fraction roots; compare x and y using the five standard relations (> ≥ < ≤ / cannot be established)
Missing number series built on differences of squares/cubes, alternate ×n +k, or ×n with increasing n
Approximation: decimals close to whole numbers in %, ×, ÷, √ and powers; find the nearest value
Arithmetic word problem on profit & loss / discount with two-step conditions
Time & work / pipes: efficiencies combined, one leaves after some days, or an emptying pipe
Trains crossing poles/platforms/each other, relative speed, or average speed of a round trip
Arithmetic word problem combining SI and CI on related sums, or splitting a sum between two rates
Linear row (7–9 persons, all facing one direction), sometimes with vacant seats or an attribute; 3–5 questions on positions, neighbours and 'how many between'
Circular table (8 persons) with a second attribute such as profession or city; facing directions sometimes mixed
Floor-based puzzle (5–8 floors, sometimes two flats per floor) with a second attribute such as colour/city/fruit
Scheduling puzzle with months and two dates per month (or days and shifts); 30/31-day month clues
Box stacking: boxes placed one above another, with colour/item attribute and 'how many boxes between' clues
Year/age-based puzzle: birth years tied to ages computed from a reference year
Square/rectangular table with persons at corners facing the centre and at mid-sides facing outward
Syllogism with 2–3 statements and two conclusions, including 'possibility' conclusions; standard five options
Syllogism with 'Only a few' or 'No' statements where a definite 'All' conclusion is the trap
Direct inequality: two or three combined statements, two conclusions to check
Blood relation chain or 'pointing to a photograph' statement; gender ambiguity is the usual trap
Direction & distance: a person walks a path with left/right turns; find the shortest distance and direction from start
Point-based direction: several points given relative to each other; find direction/distance between two of them
Letter coding: word coded by letter shifts / reversal / opposite letters; code a new word
Sentence (Chinese) coding: three or four phrases coded in two-letter codes; find the code of a word by elimination
Order & ranking within the miscellaneous block: positions from both ends, persons between two people
Data sufficiency with two statements on seating/coding/blood relation; standard five options
Statement–assumption (implicit/not implicit), standard five options
Statement–inference / course of action / cause–effect
Letter/number series in reasoning: find the missing term or next group
RBI Act/BR Act provisions and monetary-policy instruments (MPC, LAF corridor, CRR, SLR, OMO)
Recent RBI regulatory frameworks and circulars (PCA, KYC, digital lending, ombudsman, deposit/nominee rules)
Payment systems and digital currency (UPI, NPCI, RTGS/NEFT timings, e-Rupee)
Banking terms and prudential norms (NPA, CRAR, Basel III buffers, LCR/NSFR)
Economy concepts and data sources (GDP, inflation indices, publishing agencies)
Financial-sector laws and market regulators (SARFAESI, IBC, SEBI/IRDAI/PFRDA roles)
External sector: forex, FDI routes, current account, exchange-rate terms

resources.notes: RBI does not publish Phase I objective papers or answer keys; candidates receive their marks after each phase. Notifications, syllabus and results are on opportunities.rbi.org.in (Current Vacancies / Results). Previous papers in circulation are memory-based compilations by coaching institutes; RBI publications (Annual Report, Monetary Policy Statements, Financial Stability Report) are the main official sources for GA and Phase II.

questions.question: Under which section of the RBI Act, 1934 is the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) constituted?
questions.explanation: Section 45ZB provides for the constitution of the MPC; Section 45ZA deals with the inflation target.

questions.question: Under the flexible inflation targeting framework that came into effect in 2016, the CPI inflation target set for the RBI was:
questions.explanation: The target was 4% CPI inflation with an upper tolerance of 6% and a lower tolerance of 2%.

questions.question: How many members does the RBI's Monetary Policy Committee have, and who has the casting vote in case of a tie?
options: Six; the Deputy Governor in charge of monetary policy
questions.explanation: The MPC has six members (three from RBI, three external); the Governor has a casting vote in a tie.

questions.question: The Standing Deposit Facility (SDF), introduced by the RBI in April 2022, functions as:
options: The floor of the LAF corridor
The ceiling of the LAF corridor
questions.explanation: SDF, a collateral-free liquidity absorption tool, replaced the fixed-rate reverse repo as the floor of the LAF corridor; the MSF is the ceiling.

questions.question: Scheduled banks maintain the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) under which provision?
options: Section 24 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949
Section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949
questions.explanation: CRR is prescribed under Section 42 of the RBI Act, 1934; SLR is under Section 24 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.

questions.question: A term loan is classified as a Non-Performing Asset when interest or instalment of principal remains overdue for more than:
questions.explanation: Under RBI's IRAC norms, a loan becomes an NPA when interest/principal is overdue for more than 90 days.

questions.question: The SARFAESI Act, which lets secured creditors enforce security without court intervention, was enacted in which year?
questions.explanation: The Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act was enacted in 2002.

questions.question: For domestic scheduled commercial banks, the overall priority sector lending target is:
options: 40% of ANBC or CEOE, whichever is higher
questions.explanation: The overall PSL target is 40% of Adjusted Net Bank Credit or Credit Equivalent of Off-Balance Sheet Exposure, whichever is higher (18% is the agriculture sub-target).

questions.question: The Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC) is a wholly owned subsidiary of:
questions.explanation: DICGC is a wholly owned subsidiary of the RBI.

questions.question: The Unified Payments Interface (UPI) was developed by:
questions.explanation: UPI was developed and is operated by NPCI; it was launched in 2016.

questions.question: Who is the Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (as of 2026)?
questions.explanation: Sanjay Malhotra took charge as the 26th Governor of the RBI in December 2024.

questions.question: The Bank for International Settlements (BIS) is headquartered in:
questions.explanation: BIS, often called the central bank of central banks, is headquartered in Basel, Switzerland.

questions.question: The 'World Economic Outlook' report is published by:
questions.explanation: The IMF publishes the World Economic Outlook, usually in April and October.

questions.question: NABARD was established in which year?
questions.explanation: NABARD was set up on 12 July 1982 on the recommendation of the CRAFICARD (Shivaraman) committee.

questions.question: The issued capital of a Regional Rural Bank is shared by the Central Government, the State Government and the sponsor bank in the ratio:
questions.explanation: Central Government 50%, State Government 15% and sponsor bank 35%.

questions.question: Who chaired the Sixteenth Finance Commission, whose award covers 2026-27 to 2030-31?
questions.explanation: The 16th Finance Commission was constituted in December 2023 under Dr Arvind Panagariya.

questions.topic: Government Schemes & Fiscal Policy (Budget, Taxation, GST)
questions.question: The GST Council is a constitutional body under which Article?
questions.explanation: Article 279A (inserted by the 101st Amendment, 2016) provides for the GST Council. Article 280 deals with the Finance Commission.

questions.question: Under the RBI's Scale-Based Regulation framework for NBFCs, how many layers are NBFCs placed in?
questions.explanation: Four layers: Base, Middle, Upper and Top (the Top layer is ideally expected to remain empty).

questions.question: Under the RBI's revised Prompt Corrective Action (PCA) framework for banks (effective 2022), which areas are monitored?
questions.explanation: The revised PCA tracks capital, asset quality (net NPA) and leverage; profitability (return on assets) was dropped as a trigger.

questions.question: The RBI's Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, which follows a 'One Nation One Ombudsman' approach, was launched in:
questions.explanation: The Reserve Bank – Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2021 was launched in November 2021.

questions.question: To curb digital fraud, the RBI directed banks to migrate their websites to which exclusive internet domain?
questions.explanation: Banks were asked to shift to the exclusive '.bank.in' domain (registered through IDRBT); '.fin.in' was proposed for other financial entities.

questions.question: In its June 2025 policy, the RBI announced a phased cut in the Cash Reserve Ratio to:
questions.explanation: The CRR was cut by 100 basis points, from 4% to 3% of NDTL, in four equal tranches during Sep–Nov 2025.

questions.topic: Government Schemes & Fiscal Policy (Budget, Taxation, GST)
questions.question: The Income-tax Act, 2025, which replaces the Income-tax Act, 1961, comes into force from:
questions.explanation: The new Income-tax Act, 2025 takes effect from 1 April 2026 (tax year 2026-27).

questions.topic: Government Schemes & Fiscal Policy (Budget, Taxation, GST)
questions.question: Under the GST rate rationalisation effective 22 September 2025, the two main GST slabs are:
questions.explanation: The four-slab structure was replaced by two main slabs of 5% and 18%, with a special 40% rate for select luxury and sin goods.

questions.question:
Eight persons J, K, L, M, N, O, P and Q sit around a square table. Four sit at the four corners facing the centre and four sit at the middle of the four sides facing away from the centre. J sits at a corner. Q sits third to the left of J. N sits opposite J. M sits immediately to the right of J. K is an immediate neighbour of N and faces away from the centre. O faces away from the centre. L is not an immediate neighbour of M. Only one person sits between N and P.

Who sits second to the right of K?
questions.explanation: Clockwise from J (corner): J, O, L, Q, N, K, P, M. Corner-sitters face the centre (right = anticlockwise); side-sitters face outward (right = clockwise). K faces outward, so second to its right (clockwise) is M.

questions.question:
Eight persons J, K, L, M, N, O, P and Q sit around a square table. Four sit at the four corners facing the centre and four sit at the middle of the four sides facing away from the centre. J sits at a corner. Q sits third to the left of J. N sits opposite J. M sits immediately to the right of J. K is an immediate neighbour of N and faces away from the centre. O faces away from the centre. L is not an immediate neighbour of M. Only one person sits between N and P.

Who sits immediately to the left of L?
questions.explanation: Clockwise: J, O, L, Q, N, K, P, M. L sits at a corner facing the centre, so his left is clockwise — Q.

questions.question:
Eight persons J, K, L, M, N, O, P and Q sit around a square table. Four sit at the four corners facing the centre and four sit at the middle of the four sides facing away from the centre. J sits at a corner. Q sits third to the left of J. N sits opposite J. M sits immediately to the right of J. K is an immediate neighbour of N and faces away from the centre. O faces away from the centre. L is not an immediate neighbour of M. Only one person sits between N and P.

Which group consists only of persons who face away from the centre?
questions.explanation: Clockwise: J (corner), O, L (corner), Q, N (corner), K, P (corner), M. The side-sitters O, Q, K and M face away from the centre.

questions.question:
Seven persons A, B, C, D, E, F and G were born in different years among 1971, 1978, 1985, 1990, 1996, 2001 and 2008. Ages are calculated as on the same date in 2026 (age = 2026 − birth year). The sum of the ages of C and B is 73, and C is older than B. D was born in an even-numbered year, after G. A is 11 years older than D. Only one person was born between G and E (in order of birth years). F is younger than G. G was born in a year that is a multiple of 5.

What is G's age in 2026?

Seven persons A, B, C, D, E, F and G were born in different years among 1971, 1978, 1985, 1990, 1996, 2001 and 2008. Ages are calculated as on the same date in 2026 (age = 2026 − birth year). The sum of the ages of C and B is 73, and C is older than B. D was born in an even-numbered year, after G. A is 11 years older than D. Only one person was born between G and E (in order of birth years). F is younger than G. G was born in a year that is a multiple of 5.

Who was born in 1978?
questions.explanation: C + B = 73 with C older gives C–B = 55–18 or 48–25. A − D = 11 needs (41, 30) or (36, 25). D even and after G, G a multiple of 5, F after G, one person between G and E: only C 1971, E 1978, A 1985, G 1990, D 1996, F 2001, B 2008 works. E was born in 1978.

Seven persons A, B, C, D, E, F and G were born in different years among 1971, 1978, 1985, 1990, 1996, 2001 and 2008. Ages are calculated as on the same date in 2026 (age = 2026 − birth year). The sum of the ages of C and B is 73, and C is older than B. D was born in an even-numbered year, after G. A is 11 years older than D. Only one person was born between G and E (in order of birth years). F is younger than G. G was born in a year that is a multiple of 5.

What is the sum of the ages of A and F in 2026?

Eight boxes P, Q, R, S, T, U, V and W are kept one above another (position 1 is the bottom, 8 the top). Only three boxes are kept between P and T. T is kept at one of the two lowest positions. The number of boxes above V is equal to the number of boxes below P. Q is kept immediately below V. R is kept somewhere above U, and only one box is kept between R and S. W is kept adjacent to Q.

Which box is kept at the top?
questions.explanation: Bottom to top: T, W, Q, V, P, S, U, R. R is at the top.

questions.question:
Eight boxes P, Q, R, S, T, U, V and W are kept one above another (position 1 is the bottom, 8 the top). Only three boxes are kept between P and T. T is kept at one of the two lowest positions. The number of boxes above V is equal to the number of boxes below P. Q is kept immediately below V. R is kept somewhere above U, and only one box is kept between R and S. W is kept adjacent to Q.

How many boxes are kept between W and U?
questions.explanation: Bottom to top: T, W, Q, V, P, S, U, R. Between W (2) and U (7) are Q, V, P and S — four.

questions.question:
Eight boxes P, Q, R, S, T, U, V and W are kept one above another (position 1 is the bottom, 8 the top). Only three boxes are kept between P and T. T is kept at one of the two lowest positions. The number of boxes above V is equal to the number of boxes below P. Q is kept immediately below V. R is kept somewhere above U, and only one box is kept between R and S. W is kept adjacent to Q.

Which box is kept immediately above P?
questions.explanation: If T = 1, P = 5; boxes above V = boxes below P = 4, so V = 4 and Q = 3; W adjacent to Q is 2. R above U with one box between R and S gives S = 6, U = 7, R = 8. (T = 2 leads to a contradiction.) S is immediately above P.

questions.question:
Statements: Only a few banks are lenders. All lenders are institutions. No institution is a broker.
Conclusions: I. Some banks are not brokers. II. Some brokers are lenders.
questions.explanation: Banks that are lenders are institutions and hence not brokers — I follows. No lender (an institution) can be a broker — II is false.

questions.question:
Statements: All coins are notes. Some notes are cheques. No cheque is a draft.
Conclusions: I. Some coins being drafts is a possibility. II. No note is a draft.
questions.explanation: Coins are notes, and notes that are not cheques may be drafts, so coins being drafts is possible — I follows. Some notes may be drafts, so II is not definite.

questions.question:
Statements: P ≥ Q > R ≤ S; T > Q ≥ U
Conclusions: I. T > R  II. P ≥ U
questions.explanation: T > Q > R gives T > R; P ≥ Q ≥ U gives P ≥ U. Both follow.

questions.question:
Statements: A ≤ B < C = D; E > D ≥ F; G ≥ E
Conclusions: I. G > B  II. F < C
questions.explanation: G ≥ E > D = C > B gives G > B. F ≤ D = C gives only F ≤ C, so 'F < C' is not definite. Only I follows.

questions.question: In a family, L is the mother of M. M is married to N. O is the son of N. P is the sister of O. Q is the father of N. R is the wife of Q. How is R related to P?
questions.explanation: N is the child of Q and R. O and P are N's children. So R is P's grandmother.

questions.question: Point A is 12 m east of point B. Point C is 5 m north of A. Point D is 4 m west of C. Point E is 11 m south of D. How far and in which direction is E from B?
questions.explanation: Take B = (0,0): A = (12,0), C = (12,5), D = (8,5), E = (8,−6). Distance = √(8² + 6²) = 10 m, towards the South-East.

questions.question: In a certain code language, 'policy rate cut' is written as 'mi ka lo', 'rate hike likely' as 'zo lo pa' and 'cut likely soon' as 'pa mi ru'. What is the code for 'policy'?
questions.explanation: rate = lo (1 & 2), cut = mi (1 & 3), likely = pa (2 & 3). The remaining code in sentence 1, ka, means 'policy'.

questions.question:
Six persons A, B, C, D, E and F sit in a row of six seats facing north. Who sits at the extreme right end?
I. A sits third from the left end. B sits second to the right of A.
II. C sits immediately to the right of B.
options: The data in statement I alone are sufficient, but the data in statement II alone are not
The data in statement II alone are sufficient, but the data in statement I alone are not
The data in either statement I alone or statement II alone are sufficient
The data in both statements I and II together are not sufficient
The data in both statements I and II together are necessary
questions.explanation: I alone gives A = 3, B = 5 but not who is at seat 6. II alone gives no seat numbers. Together, C = 6 — so both are needed.

questions.question:
Statement: An advertisement says, 'Use our UPI app — zero charges on all transfers.'
Assumptions: I. People prefer not to pay charges on money transfers. II. No other app offers zero-charge transfers.
options: Either I or II is implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
questions.explanation: The advertisement assumes zero charges will attract users (I is implicit). It does not assume that no competitor offers the same (II is not implicit).

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the question.

When a central bank raises interest rates, the effect on inflation is neither immediate nor uniform. Higher policy rates first feed into money-market rates and bond yields; bank lending rates adjust more slowly, depending on how loans are benchmarked and how much competition banks face for deposits. Households may postpone purchases of cars and homes, and firms may defer investment, but these decisions unfold over several quarters. Meanwhile, supply shocks — a failed harvest or a spike in global oil prices — can push prices up regardless of monetary policy. This is why most central banks target inflation over a medium-term horizon and try to anchor expectations through clear communication. If people believe the central bank will act to bring inflation back to target, they are less likely to demand large wage increases or raise prices pre-emptively, which itself makes the central bank's task easier.

According to the passage, what adjusts first after a central bank raises its policy rate?
questions.explanation: 'Higher policy rates first feed into money-market rates and bond yields; bank lending rates adjust more slowly.'

Why, according to the passage, do central banks target inflation over a medium-term horizon?

Because governments require it by law

Because bond yields never respond to policy rates

questions.question:
Choose the word that best fills the blank.
The government's decision to ______ the import duty on edible oils is expected to bring relief to consumers.
questions.explanation: Only a reduction in duty lowers prices and brings relief to consumers.

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that has an error.
Not only the employees (A)/ but also the manager were (B)/ surprised by the sudden (C)/ announcement of the merger. (D)/ No error (E)
questions.explanation: With 'not only … but also', the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'the manager' (singular): 'was surprised'. Error in part B.

questions.question:
Choose the word that best fills the blank.
The minister's speech was so ______ that the audience lost interest within minutes.
questions.explanation: Losing interest within minutes implies the speech was tedious (boring); the others mean the opposite.

questions.question:
Rearrange the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.
A. Such tools, however, also raise questions about data privacy.
B. Banks are increasingly using artificial intelligence to assess loan applications.
C. Regulators are therefore drafting guidelines on how customer data may be used.
D. These systems can analyse thousands of data points in seconds.
E. This speeds up approvals and can reduce human bias.
questions.explanation: B (AI in lending) → D (capability) → E (benefit) → A ('however', privacy concern) → C ('therefore', regulation): BDEAC.

questions.question: Choose the meaning of the idiom 'to bite the bullet'.
options: To face a difficult situation with courage
questions.explanation: 'Bite the bullet' means to accept and face something unpleasant or difficult bravely.

questions.question:

Company | Revenue | Expenditure (% of revenue)

R | 400 | 85%
S | 180 | 70%

What is the total profit of all five companies?

The profit of S is what percent of the expenditure of P?
questions.explanation: Profit of S = 30% of 180 = 54; expenditure of P = 80% of 250 = 200. 54/200 × 100 = 27%.

If next year R's revenue rises by 15% and its expenditure rises by 10%, what will R's profit be?
questions.explanation: Revenue = 400 × 1.15 = 460; expenditure = 340 × 1.10 = 374. Profit = 460 − 374 = ₹86 crore.

questions.question:
Solve and compare.
I. x² − 2x − 15 = 0
II. y² + 8y + 15 = 0
options: x = y or the relationship cannot be established
questions.explanation: I: (x − 5)(x + 3) = 0 → x = 5, −3. II: (y + 3)(y + 5) = 0 → y = −3, −5. Every x is greater than or equal to every y (−3 = −3), so x ≥ y.

questions.question:
What approximate value should come in place of '?'
(19.97)² − 14.02 × 11.98 + 3.98³ ≈ ?
Find the next term: 4, 5, 14, 39, 88, ?
questions.explanation: Differences are 1², 3², 5², 7²; next 9² = 81: 88 + 81 = 169.

questions.question: ₹20,000 is invested partly at 8% and partly at 12% simple interest per annum. If the total interest after one year is ₹2,000, how much was invested at 12%?
A, B and C can finish a job in 10, 12 and 15 days respectively. All three start together, but A leaves after 2 days. In how many days in total is the job completed?
questions.explanation: Per day (in 60ths): A 6, B 5, C 4. First 2 days: 2 × 15 = 30/60. Remaining 30/60 at 9/60 per day = 10/3 days. Total = 2 + 3⅓ = 5⅓ days.

questions.question: Under the RBI's Liquidity Adjustment Facility, the Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) rate serves as:
options: The upper bound (ceiling) of the policy rate corridor
The lower bound (floor) of the policy rate corridor
The rate at which the RBI absorbs surplus liquidity overnight
The rate of interest paid on banks' CRR balances
questions.explanation: MSF is the rate at which banks can borrow overnight against excess SLR securities in emergencies; it forms the ceiling of the LAF corridor, while the Standing Deposit Facility rate is the floor.

questions.question: Banks in India maintain the Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) under which provision?
options: Section 24 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949
Section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949
questions.explanation: SLR is prescribed under Section 24 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949. Section 42 of the RBI Act covers CRR; Section 45ZB the MPC; Section 35A the RBI's power to give directions.

questions.question: Which Basel III requirement obliges banks to hold enough high-quality liquid assets to meet net cash outflows over a 30-day stress period?
questions.explanation: The LCR covers a 30-day stress horizon. The NSFR looks at stable funding over one year; the leverage ratio and capital buffers concern capital, not liquidity.

questions.question: Under the Basel III capital framework as implemented by the RBI for scheduled commercial banks, the Capital Conservation Buffer (CCB) is:
questions.explanation: The CCB, to be held in Common Equity Tier 1, is 2.5% of RWAs (fully phased in from October 2021). 5.5% is the minimum CET1 ratio and 9% the minimum total CRAR in India.

questions.question: Under the Banking Laws (Amendment) Act, 2025, a depositor can nominate up to how many persons for a deposit account?
questions.explanation: The 2025 amendment allows up to four nominees for deposit accounts, either simultaneously (in specified shares) or successively.

questions.question: The RBI launched the pilot of the retail digital rupee (e₹-R) in:
questions.explanation: The wholesale e₹ pilot began on 1 November 2022 and the retail e₹ pilot on 1 December 2022.

questions.question: The RTGS system is primarily meant for large-value transfers. What is the minimum amount that can be sent through RTGS?
questions.explanation: RTGS has a minimum of ₹2 lakh and no upper ceiling; it has been available 24×7 since December 2020. NEFT has no minimum.

questions.question: In India, the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) is compiled and released by:
options: Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT (Ministry of Commerce & Industry)
questions.explanation: WPI is released by the Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT. The NSO compiles CPI and IIP; the Labour Bureau compiles CPI for industrial workers.

questions.question: Which of the following is compiled and released by the National Statistics Office (MoSPI)?
questions.explanation: IIP is released by the NSO. WPI comes from DPIIT, the FSR and Consumer Confidence Survey from the RBI, and the PMI from a private survey provider.

questions.question: Under India's FDI policy, investment under which route does NOT need prior approval of the Government?
questions.explanation: Under the automatic route the investor only reports to the RBI after investment; the government (approval) route needs prior clearance. The FIPB itself was abolished in 2017.

questions.question: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), which set up a time-bound resolution process for stressed companies, was enacted in:
questions.explanation: The IBC was enacted in 2016. 2002 is the year of the SARFAESI Act.

questions.question: Which regulator oversees the National Pension System (NPS) and the Atal Pension Yojana?
questions.explanation: The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) regulates NPS and administers APY. EPFO runs the employees' provident fund, not NPS.

questions.topic: Government Schemes & Fiscal Policy (Budget, Taxation, GST)
questions.question: Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY), the national mission for financial inclusion, was launched on:
questions.explanation: PMJDY was launched on 28 August 2014. 9 May 2015 is the launch date of APY, PMJJBY and PMSBY.

questions.topic: Government Schemes & Fiscal Policy (Budget, Taxation, GST)
questions.question: Under the Atal Pension Yojana, subscribers receive a guaranteed minimum monthly pension after age 60 in the range of:
questions.explanation: APY offers a guaranteed monthly pension of ₹1,000, 2,000, 3,000, 4,000 or 5,000 depending on the contribution.

questions.topic: Government Schemes & Fiscal Policy (Budget, Taxation, GST)
questions.question: In government finance, the 'fiscal deficit' is best defined as:
options: Total expenditure minus total receipts excluding borrowings and other liabilities
The excess of imports over exports
questions.explanation: Fiscal deficit = total expenditure − (revenue receipts + non-debt capital receipts), i.e. the government's borrowing requirement. The second option is the revenue deficit and the third the primary deficit.

questions.topic: Government Schemes & Fiscal Policy (Budget, Taxation, GST)
questions.question: Under the Unified Pension Scheme (UPS) for central government employees, effective 1 April 2025, the assured pension for 25 years of qualifying service is what share of the average basic pay of the last 12 months before superannuation?
questions.explanation: UPS assures 50% of the average basic pay drawn over the last 12 months, for a minimum qualifying service of 25 years.

questions.question: The Kisan Credit Card scheme was introduced in 1998 on the recommendations of which committee?
questions.explanation: The KCC scheme (1998) followed the R. V. Gupta Committee on agricultural credit; it was prepared by NABARD.

questions.question: The Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI), set up in 1990, was originally established as a wholly owned subsidiary of:
questions.explanation: SIDBI was set up on 2 April 1990 as a wholly owned subsidiary of the Industrial Development Bank of India; it was later delinked from IDBI.

questions.question: The 'Global Economic Prospects' report is published by:
questions.explanation: Global Economic Prospects is a World Bank flagship; the IMF publishes the World Economic Outlook.

questions.question: The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) is headquartered in:
questions.explanation: AIIB is based in Beijing. The New Development Bank is in Shanghai and the Asian Development Bank in Manila.

questions.question: The Urjit Patel Committee (2014) is best known for recommending:
options: A flexible inflation-targeting framework with CPI inflation as the nominal anchor
Setting up payments banks and small finance banks
Merger of public sector banks into fewer large banks
The economic capital framework of the RBI
questions.explanation: The Expert Committee to Revise and Strengthen the Monetary Policy Framework (Urjit Patel, 2014) recommended CPI-based flexible inflation targeting. The economic capital framework was the Bimal Jalan Committee (2019).

questions.question: Who is the Director-General of the World Trade Organization (as of 2026)?
questions.explanation: Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala began her second term as WTO Director-General in September 2025. Georgieva heads the IMF and Banga the World Bank; Azevêdo was her predecessor.

questions.question: Which country holds the chairship of BRICS for 2026?
questions.explanation: India took over the BRICS chairship for 2026 from Brazil, which chaired the grouping in 2025.

questions.question: The 30th Conference of the Parties (COP30) to the UNFCCC was held in November 2025 in:
questions.explanation: COP30 was hosted in Belém, Brazil. COP29 was in Baku, COP28 in Dubai and COP27 in Sharm el-Sheikh.

questions.question:
Eight persons A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H sit around a circular table, all facing the centre. Each has a different profession — Banker, Doctor, Engineer, Lawyer, Pilot, Teacher, Writer and Chef.
B is the Teacher and sits exactly opposite A. The Chef sits immediately to the right of B. The Doctor sits immediately to the right of the Chef. C is not the Chef. D sits second to the left of B. The Writer sits exactly opposite the Doctor. F sits immediately to the left of D. H is an immediate neighbour of B but is not the Chef. The Pilot sits immediately to the right of the Doctor. The Banker sits immediately to the left of the Teacher. F is not the Lawyer. E sits immediately to the right of C.

Who is the Writer?
questions.explanation: Clockwise from A: A (Lawyer), E (Pilot), C (Doctor), G (Chef), B (Teacher), H (Banker), D (Writer), F (Engineer). Facing the centre, left is clockwise and right anticlockwise. D is the Writer.

questions.question:
Eight persons P, Q, R, S, T, U, V and W have birthdays in four months — February, April, August and November — of the same year, on either the 11th or the 24th of the month. No two persons share a birthday.
T's birthday is on the 11th of a month that has 30 days. Only three persons have birthdays between T and P, and P's birthday comes before T's. Q's birthday is immediately after T's. Only one person has a birthday between Q and W. R's birthday is in the same month as W's. V's birthday is in a month that has fewer than 30 days. U's birthday is on the 24th. S's birthday comes before V's.

Whose birthday is on 24 April?
questions.explanation: Feb 11 – S, Feb 24 – V, Apr 11 – P, Apr 24 – U, Aug 11 – R, Aug 24 – W, Nov 11 – T, Nov 24 – Q. (T in April is impossible because P must come four places before T.)

questions.question:
Statements: Some banks are NBFCs. All NBFCs are lenders. Only a few lenders are brokers.
Conclusions: I. Some banks are lenders. II. Some brokers are not lenders.
questions.explanation: Banks that are NBFCs are lenders, so I follows. 'Only a few lenders are brokers' says some lenders are not brokers; it says nothing definite about brokers outside lenders, so II does not follow.

questions.question:
Statements: Only a few rates are cuts. No cut is a hike. All hikes are pauses.
Conclusions: I. Some pauses are not cuts. II. Some rates are not hikes.
questions.explanation: Hikes are pauses and no hike is a cut, so the pauses that are hikes are not cuts — I follows. The rates that are cuts cannot be hikes, so II follows. Both follow.

questions.question:
Statements: L ≥ M > N ≤ O; P < N; Q ≥ O
Conclusions: I. M > O  II. Q > P
questions.explanation: M > N ≤ O gives no relation between M and O, so I does not follow. Q ≥ O ≥ N > P gives Q > P, so II follows.

questions.question: In a certain code, each vowel in a word is replaced by the next letter of the English alphabet and each consonant by the previous letter, and then the letters are written in reverse order. How is 'CREDIT' written in this code?
questions.explanation: C → B, R → Q, E → F, D → C, I → J, T → S gives BQFCJS; reversed: SJCFQB.

questions.question: A is the mother of B. B is married to C. D, who is unmarried, is the only brother of C. E is the son of B and C. F is the father of D. G is the wife of F. How is F related to B?
questions.explanation: F is the father of D, and D is C's brother, so F is C's father. B is married to C, so F is B's father-in-law.

questions.question: Point P is 9 m east of point Q. Point R is 12 m north of P. Point S is 9 m west of R. Point T is 5 m south of S. How far and in which direction is T from Q?

In which direction is point X with respect to point Y?
I. X is 5 m north of point Z, and Z is 3 m west of Y.
II. Y is 4 m south of point W, and W is 3 m east of X.
options: The data in statement I alone are sufficient, but the data in statement II alone are not
The data in statement II alone are sufficient, but the data in statement I alone are not
The data in either statement I alone or statement II alone are sufficient
The data in both statements I and II together are not sufficient
The data in both statements I and II together are necessary
questions.explanation: I: X = Y + (−3, 5) → North-West. II: W = X + (3, 0) and Y = W + (0, −4), so X = Y + (−3, 4) → North-West. Each statement alone is sufficient.

questions.question:
Statement: A bank's notice says, 'Open a deposit under our new savings scheme before 31 March to earn a higher rate of interest.'
Assumptions: I. Some customers would like to earn a higher rate of interest. II. The bank expects some customers to open deposits before 31 March.
options: Either I or II is implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
questions.explanation: The offer only makes sense if customers value higher interest (I) and if the bank expects some of them to act before the deadline (II). Both are implicit.

questions.question:
Statement: Cases of digital payment fraud have risen sharply in small towns over the past year.
Courses of action: I. Banks should run fraud-awareness campaigns in local languages in these towns. II. Digital payments should be banned in small towns.
Which course(s) of action logically follow(s)?
questions.explanation: I addresses the problem practically. II is an extreme step that would hurt genuine users and does not follow.

questions.question: In a row of 50 persons facing north, A is 18th from the left end and B is 25th from the right end. How many persons sit between A and B?
questions.explanation: B is 50 − 25 + 1 = 26th from the left. Persons between = 26 − 18 − 1 = 7.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the question.

For decades, Indian households kept the bulk of their savings in bank deposits, gold and property. That pattern is changing. Monthly contributions to mutual funds through systematic investment plans have climbed steadily, and the number of individual investors with demat accounts has multiplied. Optimists see this as a sign of financial deepening: savings that once lay idle in gold or were locked into real estate are being channelled into companies that need capital to grow.

The shift, however, carries risks that are easy to overlook in a rising market. Many new investors have never experienced a prolonged downturn, and surveys suggest that a significant share expect returns far above what equities have historically delivered. If prices fall sharply, disappointed savers may withdraw in panic, crystallising losses and souring an entire generation on markets. Banks face a quieter challenge: as deposits grow more slowly than loans, they must either raise deposit rates, which squeezes their margins, or rely on costlier wholesale funding.

None of this argues for reversing the trend. A household sector that participates in capital markets can make an economy more resilient, provided participation rests on understanding rather than exuberance. Regulators have therefore emphasised suitability — ensuring that products sold to an investor match that person's needs and capacity to bear risk — alongside clearer disclosure of costs and past performance.

Which of the following best expresses the author's main argument?
options: Households should return to bank deposits and gold because markets are too risky
The movement of household savings into markets is welcome, but it must rest on investor understanding while its side-effects on banks are managed
Rising mutual fund inflows have solved the funding problems of Indian banks
Regulators should restrict new investors from entering the equity market
Equity returns in India have always exceeded investors' expectations
questions.explanation: The author calls the shift 'financial deepening', warns of investor over-optimism and bank funding pressure, and concludes that participation must rest on understanding — not that it should be reversed or restricted.

questions.explanation: Para 2: 'as deposits grow more slowly than loans, they must either raise deposit rates … or rely on costlier wholesale funding'.

questions.explanation: I follows from the survey finding; III from 'souring an entire generation on markets'. II contradicts 'None of this argues for reversing the trend'.

What does 'crystallising' mean as used in the phrase 'crystallising losses'?
options: Making them definite by selling at a lower price
questions.explanation: Selling in panic turns paper (notional) losses into actual, realised losses — the losses become definite. 'Forming crystals' is the literal, out-of-context meaning.

questions.question:
Choose the word that best fills the blank.
The committee's report, though running to several hundred pages, was criticised for being too ______ to guide actual policy decisions.
questions.explanation: 'Though' sets up a contrast with the report's length: despite being long, it was too vague to guide decisions. The other words would be praise, not criticism.

questions.question: Which of the following sentences is grammatically correct?
options: The number of applicants have doubled since last year.
Not only the auditor but also the directors were present at the meeting.
Scarcely had the meeting begun than the power failed.
He, along with his partners, are responsible for the loss.
She has been working in the bank since five years.
questions.explanation: With 'not only … but also', the verb agrees with the nearer subject ('directors' → were). Errors in the others: 'the number … has'; 'scarcely … when'; 'He, along with … is'; 'for five years'.

questions.question:
Choose the pair of words that best fills both blanks.
The new framework seeks to ______ innovation in digital lending while ______ borrowers against predatory practices.
questions.explanation: A regulatory framework would aim to encourage innovation while protecting borrowers; in every other pair at least one word contradicts the purpose stated by 'against predatory practices'.

questions.question:
Rearrange the sentences to form a coherent paragraph and choose the FOURTH sentence.
A. Persistent inflation of this kind can, over time, also drag down the external value of the currency.
B. When a government runs persistent deficits, it may be tempted to finance them by printing money.
C. Such monetisation increases the money supply faster than the output of goods and services.
D. Central bank independence is designed precisely to remove this temptation.
E. The result is rising inflation, which erodes the real value of savings.
questions.explanation: Order: B (temptation) – C ('such monetisation') – E (result: inflation) – A ('persistent inflation of this kind', currency falls) – D (independence removes 'this temptation'). The fourth sentence is A.

questions.question:
Choose the most appropriate meaning of the idiom used in the sentence.
With inflation still uncertain, the central bank decided to keep its powder dry.
options: to avoid spending any money at all
to give up the fight against inflation
to remain prepared to act later rather than act now
to act hastily without waiting for data
